The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).

Bot authors asked for three things:

> As a bot author, I don't want my bot to end up in every open room. I want to
> choose the rooms it joins.

> As a bot author whose bot serves everyone, I don't want to add it to each
> open room by hand.

> As a bot author, I want to know when my bot lands in a new room, so it can
> say hello.

So bots no longer join open rooms by default. People still do.

The bot form (new and edit) gets a new switch:

- "Add to all open rooms" (off by default)

When the switch is on, the bot is a member of every open room: the ones that exist when the switch is turned on, and every open room that appears later. Turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships.

Whenever a bot is added to a room—automatically or by a person—its webhook receives a `joined` event, exactly once per room:

```json
{
  "event": "joined",
  "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5/42-Xy3abc9defGh/messages" }
}
```

Direct conversations never trigger `joined`. The bot may reply to `joined` the same way as to `mention`: a `200` text or HTML reply is posted into that room as the bot's message.

# Campfire

Campfire is a web-based chat application. It supports many of the features you'd
expect, including:

- Multiple rooms, with access controls
- Direct messages
- File attachments with previews
- Search
- Notifications (via Web Push)
- @mentions

## Running your own Campfire instance

Campfire's Docker image contains everything needed for a fully-functional,
single-machine deployment. This includes the web app, background jobs, caching,
file serving, and SSL. You can use our pre-built image at
`ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire:latest`, or build your own from this repo.

### Deploying with ONCE

The easiest way to self-host Campfire is with [ONCE](https://github.com/basecamp/once).
It will guide you through the initial set up and then keep your instance up to date automatically.

If you don't already have `once` installed, run this on the machine you want to run Campfire on:

```sh
curl https://get.once.com | sh
```

`once` will launch as soon as the install is finished. 

Choose Campfire from the list of applications, follow the instructions, and ONCE will take care of the rest.

If you prefer the command line to the dashboard, you can deploy directly:

```sh
once deploy ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire --host chat.example.com
```

### Deploying with Docker

If you'd rather run the Docker image yourself, you can read more about that in the [self-hosting guide](docs/self-hosting.md).

> [!TIP]
> When you start Campfire for the first time, you'll be guided through a wizard to create an admin account.
> The email address that you enter for the admin account will be visible on the sign-in page, it's there so
> that people have someone to contact if they need help with their account. If that bothers you, put in any
> email address you want and create yourself a new admin account.

## Development

You are welcome - and encouraged - to modify Campfire to your liking.
Please see our [development guide](docs/development.md) for how to get Campfire set up for local development.

## Security

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for how to report a vulnerability and a description of our trust model.

  "output_head": "# Bots

Bots are chat members that post via an HTTP API. They are implemented as `User`
records with a `bot_token` (the "Bot code" credential) and a `created_by`
owner.

## Why users?

Rooms, messages, memberships, broadcasts and push notifications all key off
`User`. By making a bot a `User`:

- `User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms` auto-joins new bots to all open rooms,
  exactly like a new human.
- Room membership forms (`User.active.ordered`) already list bots, so bots can
  be added to closed rooms the same way as people.
- `Message` with `creator: bot` broadcasts (`broadcast_create`) and enqueues
  `Room::PushMessageJob` via `Room#receive`, identical to human messages.
- Avatars reuse `User::Avatar` and `fresh_user_avatar_path`.

Human vs bot: `User.bots` (`bot_token NOT NULL`), `User.humans`
(`bot_token NULL`). Account member lists use `humans` so bots don't appear as
people; room lists keep `active` so bots are selectable.

## Ownership

`users.created_by_id` points to the creator. `BotsController#bots_scope`
returns `Current.user.created_bots` for members and `User.bots` for admins.
`User#bot?` / `#human?` helpers gate validations:

- `bot_token` uniqueness, auto-generated (`SecureRandom.hex(20)`) when
  `created_by` is present.
- Random `password` so `password_digest NOT NULL` stays satisfied; bots have
  `email_address = nil` and can't sign in.
- `name` presence required for bots.

Deleting a bot destroys its `User` row, so its `bot_token` no longer resolves
and the API returns `401 Unauthorized`.

## HTTP API

`POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_token/messages` (`BotMessagesController#create`,
unauthenticated + `skip_forgery_protection`):

- `404` if room not found (checked first).
- `401` if `bot_token` unknown or bot not `active?`.
- Raw request body (`request.raw_post`) becomes the message body; `curl -d`
  sends `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` but `raw_post` preserves the exact
  bytes. Blank (including whitespace-only) → `422` with no body.
- Otherwise `room.messages.create_with_attachment!(creator: bot, body:)`,
  `broadcast_create`, `201` with `Location: /messages/:id`.

`create_with_attachment!` + `broadcast_create` mirrors
`MessagesController#create`, so search indexing, unread rooms, Action Cable
and web push behave identically.

## UI

- `/account/edit` links to `/bots` via icon + visible "Set up chat bots"
  (nav `aria-label` + panel button).
- `resources :bots, except: :show` → `/bots`, `/bots/new`, `/bots/:id/edit`.
- Index lists each bot in one `<li>` with name, readonly `Bot code` input and
  `Edit <name>` link; "Add a chat bot" → new. No pagination.
- `_form` has optional avatar file field, `Name the bot` label + placeholder,
  and visible `Save changes` button. Edit reuses the form plus
  `Delete this chat bot` (`data-turbo-confirm` → native `confirm()`).

## Webhooks (bot mentions)

Bots may have an optional `users.webhook_url`. `_form` exposes it as
`Webhook URL` (`url_field`, optional, blank clears to `nil`);
`BotsController#bot_params` permits `:webhook_url`. `User#normalize_webhook_url`
strips blanks to `nil`; `webhook_url_must_be_valid_http_url` requires
`http(s)://` + host when present (private/local hosts allowed so bots can
point at test rigs).

`@`-mention autocomplete (`Autocompletable::UsersController`, `active`
scope) already returns bots like people (room-scoped by membership, global
otherwise), so no filtering change was needed.

Whenever a message mentions a bot, `Message#mentioned_bots` (attachables
`grep(User)` → `User.bots` with webhook, excluding self-mention
`creator_id`) enqueues one `BotWebhookJob.perform_later(message_id, bot_id)`
per bot in `after_create_commit`. Enqueue-only keeps posting fast; the HTTP
`POST` happens in the job.

`BotWebhookPayload#to_h` builds the `mention` event:

- `author` from `message.creator` (`id`, `name`).
- `room.reply_to` is the bot's own posting URL
  `/rooms/:room_id/:bot_token/messages` (no named route exists for the
  `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_token/messages` endpoint, so built manually).
- `message.body.text` is `body.to_plain_text` with the bot's own
  `@<name>` stripped (`gsub` + `strip`); per-bot so multi-bot mentions each
  get their own command.
- `message.body.html` is `body.to_s` (full `<div class="trix-content">…`
  rich-text, including `<action-text-attachment>` mention markup).
- `message.link` is `room_at_message_path(room, message.id)`
  (`/rooms/:room_id/@:message_id` deep link). Paths are relative.

`BotWebhookJob` `POST`s JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`, 10s
open/read timeouts) and handles the reply:

- `204` → nothing.
- `200` with `text/plain` or `text/html` (charset suffix ignored) and
  non-blank body → `room.messages.create_with_attachment!(creator: bot,
  body:)` + `broadcast_create`, mirroring `BotMessagesController`.
- Anything else → ignored. All failures logged, never raised, so a dead
  webhook can't break posting.

    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      Membership.insert_all(Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } })

    end

        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end

      order(:created_at).first

  end

  end

    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type

class BotWebhookJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :default

  def perform(message_id, bot_id)
    message = Message.find_by(id: message_id)
    bot = User.bots.find_by(id: bot_id)
    return unless message && bot
    return if bot.webhook_url.blank?
    return unless bot.active?

    payload = BotWebhookPayload.new(message: message, bot: bot).to_h
    response = post_json(bot.webhook_url, payload)
    handle_response(response, message.room, bot)
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.error "BotWebhookJob failed for message #{message_id} bot #{bot_id}: #{e.class} #{e.message}"
  end

  private
    def post_json(url, payload)
      uri = URI.parse(url)
      http = Net::HTTP.new(uri.host, uri.port)
      http.use_ssl = (uri.scheme == "https")
      http.open_timeout = 10
      http.read_timeout = 10
      path = uri.request_uri.presence || "/"
      request = Net::HTTP::Post.new(path, { "Content-Type" => "application/json" })
      request.body = payload.to_json
      http.request(request)
    end

    def handle_response(response, room, bot)
      return unless response

      case response.code.to_i
      when 204
        nil
      when 200
        content_type = response["Content-Type"].to_s.split(";").first.to_s.strip.downcase
        if %w[ text/plain text/html ].include?(content_type)
          body = response.body.to_s.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
          if body.strip.present?
            reply = room.messages.create_with_attachment!(creator: bot, body: body)
            reply.broadcast_create
          end
        end
      else
        nil
      end
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.error "BotWebhookJob response handling failed: #{e.class} #{e.message}"
    end

  included do
    scope :connected,    -> { where(connected_at: CONNECTION_TTL.ago..) }
    scope :disconnected, -> { where(connected_at: [ nil, ...CONNECTION_TTL.ago ]) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def disconnect_all
      connected.update_all connected_at: nil, connections: 0, updated_at: Time.current
    end

    def connect(membership, connections)
      where(id: membership.id).update_all(connections: connections, connected_at: Time.current, unread_at: nil)
    end
  end

  def connected?
    connected_at? && connected_at >= CONNECTION_TTL.ago
  end

  def present
    self.class.connect(self, connected? ? connections + 1 : 1)
  end

  def connected
    increment_connections
    touch :connected_at
  end

  def disconnected
    decrement_connections
    update! connected_at: nil if connections < 1
  end

  def refresh_connection
    increment_connections unless connected?
    touch :connected_at
  end

  def increment_connections
    connected? ? increment!(:connections, touch: true) : update!(connections: 1)
  end

  def decrement_connections
    connected? ? decrement!(:connections, touch: true) : update!(connections: 0)

require "net/http"
require "uri"

class BotWebhookJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :default

  def perform(message_id, bot_id)
    message = Message.find_by(id: message_id)
    bot = User.bots.find_by(id: bot_id)
    return unless message && bot
    return if bot.webhook_url.blank?
    return unless bot.active?

    payload = BotWebhookPayload.new(message: message, bot: bot).to_h
    response = post_json(bot.webhook_url, payload)
    handle_response(response, message.room, bot)
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.error "BotWebhookJob failed for message #{message_id} bot #{bot_id}: #{e.class} #{e.message}"
  end

  private
    def post_json(url, payload)
      uri = URI.parse(url)
      http = Net::HTTP.new(uri.host, uri.port)
      http.use_ssl = (uri.scheme == "https")
      http.open_timeout = 10
      http.read_timeout = 10
      path = uri.request_uri.presence || "/"
      request = Net::HTTP::Post.new(path, { "Content-Type" => "application/json" })
      request.body = payload.to_json
      http.request(request)
    end

    def handle_response(response, room, bot)
      return unless response

      case response.code.to_i
      when 204
        nil
      when 200
        content_type = response["Content-Type"].to_s.split(";").first.to_s.strip.downcase
        if %w[ text/plain text/html ].include?(content_type)
          body = response.body.to_s.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
          if body.strip.present?
            reply = room.messages.create_with_attachment!(creator: bot, body: body)
            reply.broadcast_create
          end
        end
      else
        nil
      end
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.error "BotWebhookJob response handling failed: #{e.class} #{e.message}"
    end

    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      users = Array(users)
      return if users.empty?

      existing_ids = Membership.where(room_id: room.id, user_id: user_ids).pluck(:user_id)
      new_ids = user_ids - existing_ids
      return if new_ids.empty?

      room.notify_bots_joined(new_ids)
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end

  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do

      order(:created_at).first

      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)
    end

Bots are chat members that post via an HTTP API. They are implemented as `User`
records with a `bot_token` (the "Bot code" credential) and a `created_by`
owner.

## Why users?

Rooms, messages, memberships, broadcasts and push notifications all key off
`User`. By making a bot a `User`:

- `User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms` auto-joins new bots to all open rooms,
  exactly like a new human.
- Room membership forms (`User.active.ordered`) already list bots, so bots can
  be added to closed rooms the same way as people.
- `Message` with `creator: bot` broadcasts (`broadcast_create`) and enqueues
  `Room::PushMessageJob` via `Room#receive`, identical to human messages.
- Avatars reuse `User::Avatar` and `fresh_user_avatar_path`.

Human vs bot: `User.bots` (`bot_token NOT NULL`), `User.humans`
(`bot_token NULL`). Account member lists use `humans` so bots don't appear as
people; room lists keep `active` so bots are selectable.

## Ownership

`users.created_by_id` points to the creator. `BotsController#bots_scope`
returns `Current.user.created_bots` for members and `User.bots` for admins.
`User#bot?` / `#human?` helpers gate validations:

- `bot_token` uniqueness, auto-generated (`SecureRandom.hex(20)`) when
  `created_by` is present.
- Random `password` so `password_digest NOT NULL` stays satisfied; bots have
  `email_address = nil` and can't sign in.
- `name` presence required for bots.

Deleting a bot destroys its `User` row, so its `bot_token` no longer resolves
and the API returns `401 Unauthorized`.

## HTTP API

`POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_token/messages` (`BotMessagesController#create`,
unauthenticated + `skip_forgery_protection`):

- `404` if room not found (checked first).
- `401` if `bot_token` unknown or bot not `active?`.
- Raw request body (`request.raw_post`) becomes the message body; `curl -d`
  sends `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` but `raw_post` preserves the exact
  bytes. Blank (including whitespace-only) → `422` with no body.
- Otherwise `room.messages.create_with_attachment!(creator: bot, body:)`,
  `broadcast_create`, `201` with `Location: /messages/:id`.

`create_with_attachment!` + `broadcast_create` mirrors
`MessagesController#create`, so search indexing, unread rooms, Action Cable
and web push behave identically.

## UI

- `/account/edit` links to `/bots` via icon + visible "Set up chat bots"
  (nav `aria-label` + panel button).
- `resources :bots, except: :show` → `/bots`, `/bots/new`, `/bots/:id/edit`.
- Index lists each bot in one `<li>` with name, readonly `Bot code` input and
  `Edit <name>` link; "Add a chat bot" → new. No pagination.
- `_form` has optional avatar file field, `Name the bot` label + placeholder,
  and visible `Save changes` button. Edit reuses the form plus
  `Delete this chat bot` (`data-turbo-confirm` → native `confirm()`).

## Webhooks (bot mentions)

Bots may have an optional `users.webhook_url`. `_form` exposes it as
`Webhook URL` (`url_field`, optional, blank clears to `nil`);
`BotsController#bot_params` permits `:webhook_url`. `User#normalize_webhook_url`
strips blanks to `nil`; `webhook_url_must_be_valid_http_url` requires
`http(s)://` + host when present (private/local hosts allowed so bots can
point at test rigs).

`@`-mention autocomplete (`Autocompletable::UsersController`, `active`
scope) already returns bots like people (room-scoped by membership, global
otherwise), so no filtering change was needed.

Whenever a message mentions a bot, `Message#mentioned_bots` (attachables
`grep(User)` → `User.bots` with webhook, excluding self-mention
`creator_id`) enqueues one `BotWebhookJob.perform_later(message_id, bot_id)`
per bot in `after_create_commit`. Enqueue-only keeps posting fast; the HTTP
`POST` happens in the job.

`BotWebhookPayload#to_h` builds the `mention` event:

- `author` from `message.creator` (`id`, `name`).
- `room.reply_to` is the bot's own posting URL
  `/rooms/:room_id/:bot_token/messages` (no named route exists for the
  `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_token/messages` endpoint, so built manually).
- `message.body.text` is `body.to_plain_text` with the bot's own
  `@<name>` stripped (`gsub` + `strip`); per-bot so multi-bot mentions each
  get their own command.
- `message.body.html` is `body.to_s` (full `<div class="trix-content">…`
  rich-text, including `<action-text-attachment>` mention markup).
- `message.link` is `room_at_message_path(room, message.id)`
  (`/rooms/:room_id/@:message_id` deep link). Paths are relative.

`BotWebhookJob` `POST`s JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`, 10s
open/read timeouts) and handles the reply:

- `204` → nothing.
- `200` with `text/plain` or `text/html` (charset suffix ignored) and
  non-blank body → `room.messages.create_with_attachment!(creator: bot,
  body:)` + `broadcast_create`, mirroring `BotMessagesController`.
- Anything else → ignored. All failures logged, never raised, so a dead
  webhook can't break posting.
